title: Eval result row
description: One evaluated task case, with the plan §8 field list verbatim (ws-j item 2). Rows are produced per role (plan §9: fixer-worker, review-classifier) and per (model, driver) cell of the eval matrix; comparison-table.schema.json aggregates them.

role.description: Which of the plan §9 roles produced this row.

suite.description: Name of the task suite the case came from (the `name` field of a suite.schema.json document).

case.description: id of the cases[] entry this row scored (links to suite.schema.json case.id). suites/README.md promises one row per case, so rows carry the case id for traceability; optional at schema grain, always emitted by the J2 runner.

model.description: The model id the wire actually served. Served-id decision (2026-09-14): the eval wires request the id the wire serves — glm-5.3-flash on the GLM coding wire, the anthropic-compat wire keeps its served id, deepseek keeps its served id — so the toolkit seam's observed-model check passes green. An observed remap despite the served id is a vendor-behavior documentation entry, not an eval failure.

passed.description: Number of scoring probes that passed for this case.

total.description: Number of scoring probes in this case (at least one).

costUSD.description: Per-invocation cost in USD, or null. DD-9 (2026-09-14): subscription lanes have no per-invocation USD, so they report null — a number is never invented for them.

costBasis.description: Optional basis of a non-null costUSD, mirroring the toolkit's WorkerResult.costBasis: "billed" is provider-reported spend, "modeled" is an estimate from published rates. It exists so a modeled number is never silently reported as actual spend, and it is forbidden when costUSD is null (DD-9).

wallTimeMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the invocation in milliseconds.

tokens.description: Token usage as observed at the toolkit seam (ADR-0001 usage shape): input/output required; cache and reasoning counters optional, all integers >= 0.

runId.description: Identifier shared by all rows produced in the same eval run.

probes.description: VERSIONED ADDITIVE change F4 (2026-09-21): per-probe observed outcomes, so a confusion matrix is computable from rows.jsonl. The runner captures one expected-verdict entry per review-classifier row (expected: the suite's expected verdict, observed: the classifier's verdict or null when missing/unparseable, passed: whether they matched); absent on old rows by design — every committed snapshot still validates. kind/expected are vocabulary-constrained (CodeRabbit bot thread T3) so a typo cannot silently drop a probe from the metrics; observed stays open because out-of-vocabulary observations are intentionally preserved.

kind.description: Which scoring probe this entry records — the review-classifier probe. Constrained to the literal (CodeRabbit bot thread T3): a typo'd kind would otherwise vanish from every classifier metric.

expected.description: The suite's expected verdict, in the classifyThreads vocabulary mirrored by schema/suite.schema.json. Constrained to the enum (CodeRabbit bot thread T3): a typo'd expected would otherwise be silently skipped by the confusion builder.

observed.description: What the worker actually produced (e.g. the observed verdict), or null when missing or unparseable — a null observed is a miss, never a match.

passed.description: Whether observed matched expected for this probe.

suspiciousBenign.description: True when the case's fixture-side label.json carries fp_flag 'suspicious-benign' (an adjudicated suspicious-but-benign negative: alarming-looking content whose expected verdict is not actionable). Absent otherwise — absence means unflagged, never false-by-default; micro suites carry no labels so their rows omit it. The FP rate on this subset is what makes classifier false-positive behavior scoreable.

invalid.description: P5 evidence marker: the row is retained but invalid because the historical fixer run did not bind the driver's workspace to the graded fixture. Marked rows are never deleted.

variant.description: VERSIONED ADDITIVE change F6 (2026-09-21): the prompt/tool-surface bundle id of the suite this row ran under. Omitted when the suite declares none (the default posture), so pre-F6 rows and default-posture rows keep their exact shape.

expectedCases.description: VERSIONED ADDITIVE change W6.2 (2026-09-25): the declared case count of the suite this row ran (suite.schema.json cases[] length). Carried by EVERY row so coverage parity is computable from rows.jsonl alone: the cases a run budget gated before dispatch have no rows by design (a fabricated zero would claim a verdict that never ran), so the coverage denominator must ride the rows that did run. comparison-table.schema.json aggregates it into each cell's expectedCases/coveredCases/coverage columns. Absent on all pre-W6.2 rows by design — every committed snapshot still validates, and a regrade of old rows reproduces its original tables.

stopCause.description: VERSIONED ADDITIVE change W6.2 (2026-09-25): the cause a dispatched case's row is incomplete evidence. 'budget' = the driver stopped the case on its budget (per-case USD/token cap): the row stays an honest incomplete outcome (score 0 over the configured probe ceiling, journal status budget-exhausted) — never a fabricated completion, never a silent absence — but it does not count toward a cell's coveredCases, because a budget stop breaks coverage parity (RS-9 §1.3). Absent = the row is the case's complete evidence. The vocabulary is closed so a future cause (e.g. a bounded-retry timeout class) must extend it deliberately.
